classification_policy.conductor: Exact source_name is named by an authoritative addElectricWires invocation.
classification_policy.insulator: Exact source_name is a concrete member of the authoritative ANY.Rubber insulation group.
classification_policy.insulator_group: Exact source_name is the name-only ANY.Rubber technical group.
classification_policy.not_applicable: The source record is named by neither direct electrical registration nor the direct insulation group. Names, generic WIRES generation tags, and OreDict wire/cable registrations are not promoted to electrical evidence.

cable_domain.representation_projection: Only gate-registered cable forms with an exact electrical_by_specification entry become conductor blocks. The three non-electric single cable forms remain MaterialItems.

runtime_domain.persistence_difference: GT6 does not serialize mBurnCounter. CrucibleCraft persists the counter and decay phase so chunk unloading cannot clear overload damage.

selected.rule: Preserve max_voltage as the packet ceiling. A display tier may be derived from the pinned GT6 voltage table, but it does not replace or round the exact limit.

voltage_tiers.question: How do exact GT6 maximum voltages map to CrucibleCraft machine/network tiers?

selected.rule: Each traversed cable block subtracts its exact loss_per_meter from packet voltage before forwarding. A packet whose magnitude is not greater than the loss stops at that block.

loss_per_segment.question: What constitutes a CrucibleCraft cable segment and when is the source EU-per-block loss applied?

selected.rule: Forward first, then record downstream-used amperage for this segment. If post-loss voltage exceeds max_voltage or same-tick aggregate amperage exceeds max_amperage, increment burn and report the full offered amperage upstream so the excess is dissipated. Counter 16 schedules fire; one point decays every 512 ticks.

overvoltage_behavior.question: Does overvoltage reject transfer, accumulate damage, burn cable, explode, or use another reviewed behavior?

selected.rule: Plan each injection over loaded connected neighbors in stable Direction order with a per-injection visited set; do not persist a global graph or load chunks. Execute under the existing energy conservation contract.

network_topology.question: Which graph/component model, update schedule, split/merge behavior, and persistence boundaries will cable networks use?

selected.rule: Map cable/double/quadruple/octuple/dodecuple cable to source gauges 1/2/4/8/12 and preserve exact amperage multiplication. Other source wire gauges are outside the first T6 vertical.

gauge_mapping.question: Will the five current cable forms use GT6's exact amperage multipliers, and how are unsupported source wire gauges represented?

selected.rule: Generate one block only for each source-backed registered material/gauge pair and encode six connections as blockstate booleans. T6a is 115 cable blocks and 7,360 states; three registered non-electric forms remain items.

block_representation.question: How are material and gauge identity represented without creating an unbounded registry or a mutable block-entity identity?

selected.rule: T6d adds exactly the 29 gate-registered materials with an exact wireGt01 specification. wireGt02..16 remain deferred.

bare_wire_extension.question: Which bare-wire forms are required to make source contact damage observable?

selected.rule: Persist burn counter and 512-tick decay phase while keeping the traversal graph transient. This is an explicit CrucibleCraft anti-unload-exploit difference from GT6.

burn_persistence.question: Should chunk unloading reset accumulated cable overload damage?
